title: Tree classes without fan-in bounds
statement: For a natural number $d$ and a language $L$ over Boolean strings, if $L$ is recognized by a family of Boolean circuit trees with fan-in at most two, polynomial size, and depth at most $b(\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1)^d$ at every input length $n$, for some natural number $b$, then $L$ is recognized by a family of Boolean circuit trees of polynomial size and depth at most $b'(\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1)^d$ at every input length $n$, for some natural number $b'$.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ belongs to the fan-in-two tree-circuit class with parameter $d$ (polynomial size, polylogarithmic depth, and equality of the recognized language)
